label: <DEL> delimiter step in short sequences (L <= 7)
explanation: Fires only at the delimiter step (in_tok = <DEL>, t = L, the step that outputs original token 0), and only when the sequence has 3-7 original tokens. It is silent at <DEL> for L = 8 or 9 and essentially never fires in the original or copy phases (about 25 stray activations out of 334k). Magnitude depends on length: per-activation mass peaks at L = 4 (all top activations are L = 4 sequences, about 5.5), stays high at L = 3 and 5, drops at L = 6, and is weak at L = 7 (lowest quartile is mostly L = 7). Token identity (out_tok, prev_tok, first_tok, next_out) has no effect. Rate falls slightly as the number of digits goes up, but that tracks L. Effectively a short-sequence delimiter detector.

issues: None of the claims are refuted. On the test split, (phase == 1) & (L <= 7) scores precision 1.0, recall 0.99993, F1 0.99996 and mass recall 0.9999995, with 0 false positives.

Firing outside the predicate is scattered noise. There are 25 missed steps on the test split, carrying 0.0% of the activation mass. Most sit at t=4 in the original phase of L >= 8 sequences, mainly ones that start with 'h s'-like tokens, at activation 0.00-0.02 of max. There are also a few tiny firings at <DEL> for L=8 or 9 (dev: 9 at L=8, 6 at L=9).

The full-rate claim checks out. Steps per sequence are 2L, so L=3 has 78390/6 = 13065 sequences and all 13065 fire at <DEL>, and L=7 has 83294 sequences and 83294 fire at t=7. The feature fires on effectively every <DEL> step for L 3-7 and essentially never at L 8-9.

The magnitude claim checks out. Mass per active step is roughly 3.6e-6 at L=3, 4.2e-6 at L=4 (the peak), 3.9e-6 at L=5, 2.9e-6 at L=6 and 1.1e-6 at L=7. The top activations are all L=4, and the lowest-quartile examples are L=7.

Token identity has no effect. out_tok, next_out, prev_tok and first_tok rates are flat (e.g. out_tok 0.104-0.106). The decline with n_digits comes from L, because the firing rate within the predicate region is 100%.
